title: Slopegraph name shrink stepped below the 28 px floor from odd fitted sizes
body:
## Summary
slopegraphLayout fits an often-odd font size and then shrinks by 2 guarded only by `fontSize > minFont`, so 29 px stepped to 27 px for names and ranks.

## Description
packages/viz/src/slopegraph-layout.ts:167 sets `fontSize = round(clamp(step0 * 0.62, minFont, maxFont))` (odd values 29, 31 ... are common); the shrink loop at packages/viz/src/slopegraph-layout.ts:210 then did `fontSize -= 2` while `fontSize > minFont`, landing on 27 px with overflow=false. That breaks the repo law (every readable text >= 28 px in the artboard, .claude/perfect/config.md Repo law; DESIGN.md §6.5). Fixed: each step is `Math.max(minFont, fontSize - 2)`.

## Flow
- Era slopegraph with 9 rows (fits at 29 px) and long surnames -> span < 26 % of width -> shrink loop
- 29 > 28 -> 27 -> loop exits; names and ranks render at 27 px
- fix: clamp each shrink step at minFont; test sweeps surnames 10-22 chars

## Expected impact


## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no slopegraph label below the 28 px floor
Before: 85 of 3120 sampled layouts (n 2-14, surnames 6-20, 8 heights, both formats) at 27 px; viz.test seeded red
After: 0 of 3120; viz.test green
Method: gate - red-then-green viz.test case plus the probe sweep re-run on the commit
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/viz/src/slopegraph-layout.ts:167 `let fontSize = Math.round(clamp(step0 * 0.62, minFont, maxFont));`
packages/viz/src/slopegraph-layout.ts:210-212 `while (m.span < minSpan && fontSize > minFont) { fontSize -= 2;` (pre-fix)
probe: slope fontSize<28: 85 of 3120 [27] -> 0 of 3120

title: Slopegraph said no overflow when names squeezed slopes below the min span
body:
## Summary
When font shrink and name shortening could not keep the slope span >= 26 % of the width, slopegraphLayout still returned overflow=false, even with a negative span.

## Description
packages/viz/src/slopegraph-layout.ts:197-217 shrinks the font, then falls back from full names to surnames, to keep `span >= width * 0.26`, but `overflow` (packages/viz/src/slopegraph-layout.ts:261) only covered the vertical label gap. A layout whose right axis sat LEFT of its left axis (span -111.8 px) read as fitted, so lines drew backwards and labels overlapped silently. Registry data-viz/empty-and-degraded-chart-states: a form below its structural minimum must say so rather than draw a degenerate figure. Fixed: `overflow ||= m.span < minSpan`, doc updated.

## Flow
- 6 rows with 26-char surnames at 885 px -> fontSize floors at 28 -> span -111.8 px
- overflow false -> composition tests and callers that trust the flag treat it as fitted
- fix: the span check joins the overflow flag; new test pins it

## Expected impact


## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a horizontally unfittable slopegraph is flagged
Before: span -111.8 px (min 230.1), overflow false; viz.test seeded red
After: same input -> overflow true; compositions suite unchanged
Method: gate - red-then-green viz.test case
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/viz/src/slopegraph-layout.ts:261 `overflow: spacing < minLabelGap - 1e-6 || outside,` (pre-fix)
probe: long names: span -111.8 minSpan 230.1 overflow false -> true

title: measureText re-resolved the face/weight table on every call
body:
## Summary
advances() scanned Object.keys(FONT_ADVANCES) with filter/map/reduce on every measureText call before consulting its cache; memoised per (face, weight).

## Description
packages/viz/src/text.ts:41-62 resolved the nearest-weight table key on every call; fitText/wrapText/ellipsize (packages/viz/src/text.ts:115-221) call measureText per word or per character for every candidate size, and DataRace (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/layout.ts:100-110) and the Era frame lay text out per frame. A second Map keyed `face:weight` now returns the resolved map directly; output is identical.

## Flow
- DataRace frame -> fitSlot -> fitText (up to 3 passes x ~30 sizes) -> wrapText -> measureText per word
- each measureText -> Object.keys(13).filter.map.reduce -> Map lookup
- fix: memoise the resolved map per (face, requested weight)

## Expected impact


## Evaluation
Claim: performance - measureText / fitText time on one timed path
Before: measureText x200k 158-160 ms; fitText(68-char title, 96->28 px) x300 149-157 ms
After: measureText x200k 56-59 ms; fitText x300 84-89 ms; results equal
Method: probe - tsx timing of HEAD copy vs fix on the same inputs, 3 runs each
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/viz/src/text.ts:41-49 (pre-fix) `const weights = Object.keys(FONT_ADVANCES).filter(...).map(...); const w = weights.reduce(...)` ran before `advanceMaps.get(key)`
probe2: A(HEAD) 158.4 / 149.0 ms vs B(fix) 57.8 / 83.5 ms; same: true true

title: fitText never tried the min size when max - min was odd
body:
## Summary
fitText stepped max, max-2, ... while size >= min, so an odd span skipped min and returned the min layout with fits=false even when it fit.

## Description
packages/viz/src/text.ts:207 (pre-fix) `for (let size = max; size >= min; size -= 2)`: with min 29 / max 40 the last size tried is 31, then the fallback returns fontSize 29 with fits=false without measuring it - a false 'does not fit' that tells callers to ellipsize or fail. Sizes are now max, max-2, ... plus min itself; even spans keep the exact sequence.

## Flow
- fitText('Hello world', {min: 29, max: 40, maxWidth = width at 29 px + 0.1})
- tries 40 ... 31, none fit -> returns {fontSize 29, fits: false}
- fix: append min to the candidate list

## Expected impact


## Evaluation
Claim: quality - fitText reports fits truthfully at min
Before: {fontSize 29, fits: false} for text that fits at 29; text.test seeded red
After: {fontSize 29, fits: true}
Method: gate - red-then-green text.test case
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/viz/src/text.ts:207 (pre-fix) `for (let size = max; size >= min; size -= 2)`
probe1: fitText odd { fontSize: 29, lines: [ 'Hello world' ], fits: false }

title: LineRace y-axis repeated tick labels on sub-unit steps
body:
## Summary
lineRaceLayout formatted niceTicks values with valueDecimals, so a 0.5 or 0.25 step printed duplicate labels ('0','1','1','2','2').

## Description
packages/viz/src/line-race.ts:215-219 (pre-fix) mapped every tick through `formatFixed(value, valueDecimals)`; with valueDecimals 0 and yDomain [0, 2] niceTicks returns 0/0.5/1/1.5/2 and the axis read 0, 1, 1, 2, 2 - an axis asserting two different gridlines are the same number. Registry data-viz/scale-and-axis-design: ticks land on readable round numbers in the data's unit. Now one precision per axis: max(valueDecimals, decimals of the step).

## Flow
- lineRaceLayout({yDomain: [0, 2], valueDecimals: 0}) -> niceTicks step 0.5
- labels '0','1','1','2','2'
- fix: tickDecimals = max(valueDecimals, decimalsOf(step)) -> '0.0','0.5','1.0','1.5','2.0'

## Expected impact


## Evaluation
Claim: quality - duplicate tick labels on an axis
Before: [0,2] -> 3 distinct of 5 labels; [0,1] -> 2 distinct of 5; line-race.test seeded red
After: 5 of 5 distinct on [0,2], [0,1], [0,0.3], [0,7]; [0,300] still '0','100','200','300'
Method: gate - red-then-green line-race.test case
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/viz/src/line-race.ts:215-219 (pre-fix) `label: formatFixed(value, valueDecimals)`
probe1: linerace ticks [ '0', '1', '1', '2', '2' ]

title: LineRace fallback colours were near-invisible on the light video sheet
body:
## Summary
fallbackColor hashed ids to hsl(h 62% 64%), a lightness for the retired dark theme; on the Photo Finish sheet 18 of 20 sample ids fell under 3:1.

## Description
packages/viz/src/line-race.ts:96-103 returned `hsl(${h % 360} 62% 64%)`. ADR 009 made the video ground the light timing sheet (#eceff2, packages/design-tokens/src/index.ts:54), where those lines reach 1.25-3.7:1 - under WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11's 3:1 for graphical objects. Registry data-viz/encoding-vocabulary: series colour is a meaning-bearing channel. Lightness is now 32 % (every hue >= 3.42:1); a test computes contrast for 400 ids against the sheet.

## Flow
- LineRace series without an explicit colour -> fallbackColor(id)
- yellow/green hues at L 64 % on #eceff2 -> ~1.3:1
- fix: L 32 %; test pins >= 3:1 for 400 ids

## Expected impact


## Evaluation
Claim: quality - non-text contrast of fallback series colours
Before: 18 of 20 F1 ids under 3:1, worst 1.26; all 360 hues min 1.25; test seeded red at 1.27
After: 0 of 20 under 3:1, worst 3.44; all hues min 3.42
Method: gate - red-then-green line-race.test contrast case plus the hue sweep probe
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/viz/src/line-race.ts:102 (pre-fix) `return `hsl(${h % 360} 62% 64%)`;`
packages/design-tokens/src/index.ts:54 background: "#eceff2"
probe3: ids under 3:1: 18 of 20 min 1.26 -> 0 of 20 min 3.44

title: declaredDomain nice ends lacked niceTicks' float tolerance
body:
## Summary
declaredDomain({nice}) widened an end that was already a tick multiple by a whole step and returned untidy floats, while niceTicks (same rule) used a 1e-9 tolerance and tidy().

## Description
packages/viz/src/time-scale.ts:96 (pre-fix) `[Math.floor(min / step) * step, Math.ceil(max / step) * step]`: 0.07 / 0.01 = 7.000000000000001 -> 0.08, and ends like 0.7000000000000001. packages/viz/src/ticks.ts:40-41 already guards the same division with +-1e-9 and tidies. One rounding rule, two implementations, one fixed. ticks.ts now exports tidy and declaredDomain uses the same tolerance.

## Flow
- declaredDomain([0, 0.07], {nice: true, count: 8}) -> [0, 0.08]
- fix: floor/ceil with 1e-9 tolerance + tidy()

## Expected impact


## Evaluation
Claim: quality - nice-domain overshoot and float noise
Before: probe over 14000 domains: 15 widened by a whole step, 1114 untidy ends; scale-kit.test seeded red
After: 0 widened, 0 untidy; existing nice cases unchanged
Method: gate - red-then-green scale-kit.test case plus the 14000-domain probe
Result: better
Gate: none

title: parseTime rolled impossible dates into the next month
body:
## Summary
parseTime accepted day <= 31 for every month, so '2023-02-31' became 2023-03-03 instead of NaN.

## Description
packages/viz/src/time-scale.ts:23 (pre-fix) `day > 31` was the only day check; Feb 29 in a non-leap year, Feb 31 and Apr 31 parsed as dates in the following month. Every other malformed input already returns NaN. Now the day is checked against the month's length (leap-aware).

## Flow
- parseTime('2023-02-31') -> 2023.1671 (== '2023-03-03')
- fix: days-in-month check -> NaN

## Expected impact


## Evaluation
Claim: quality - invalid dates rejected
Before: 3 of 3 impossible dates parsed to a real time; scale-kit.test seeded red
After: 3 of 3 NaN; 2024-02-29 and 2023-12-31 unchanged
Method: gate - red-then-green scale-kit.test case
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Callout let prefix, suffix and label fall below 28 px
body:
## Summary
DataClock and lineRaceLayout clamp text at 28 px, but Callout scaled prefix/suffix by their scale props and took labelFontSize verbatim.

## Description
The owner rule (every readable text >= 28 px) is enforced at packages/viz/src/DataClock.tsx:44 and packages/viz/src/line-race.ts:134, but packages/viz/src/Callout.tsx (pre-fix lines 94, 121, 124) computed `fs * prefixScale`, `fs * suffixScale` and accepted any labelFontSize. A 60 px callout with the Era's scales rendered an 18 px suffix and a 20 px label. Callout now clamps number, prefix, suffix and label at 28.

## Flow
- Callout({fontSize: 60, prefixScale: 0.4, suffixScale: 0.3, labelFontSize: 20})
- texts at 24 / 18 / 20 px
- fix: Math.max(28, ...) on each size

## Expected impact


## Evaluation
Claim: quality - min text size in Callout
Before: min 18 px; viz.test seeded red
After: min 28 px; compositions goldens unchanged
Method: gate - red-then-green viz.test case
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:

title: '→' is absent from all three video faces; Era draws it via system fallback
body:
## Summary
The generated metric table shows U+2190/U+2192 absent from Barlow Condensed, Inter and JetBrains Mono (Google latin subsets), yet the Era payoff prefix and the fixture headline set '→' in Barlow, so Chromium substitutes a system font per glyph.

## Description
packages/viz/src/font-metrics.generated.ts:16, :20, :32 - the rows for condensed, ui and mono end in 0 (glyph missing) for ← and → (the faces are Google 'latin' subsets, which carry ↑ ↓ but not ← →). packages/compositions/src/EraAdjustedFrame.tsx:279 renders `${ordinal} →` in theme.fonts.display (Barlow Condensed, then "Arial Narrow", sans-serif - packages/design-tokens/src/index.ts:10), and packages/schemas/src/fixtures.ts:29 puts '43rd → 1st' in an on_screen headline. Chromium falls back per glyph to a system face: not OFL from fonts/ (CLAUDE.md Fonts; DESIGN.md §6.5 bans desktop-EULA fonts on the render path) and not deterministic across machines - and DESIGN.md §6.3's 'render fails if document.fonts reports any fallback' only sees face loads, not per-glyph fallback. On the viz side measureText swallows the fact: a missing glyph silently becomes a 2x average width (packages/viz/src/text.ts:37, :85). Fix: viz exports `missingGlyphs(text, face, weight)` from the table it already holds; compositions replace '→' (e.g. a drawn arrow or a glyph the faces carry) and a compositions test asserts no rendered string has missing glyphs.

## Flow
- Era payoff -> Callout prefix '12TH →' in Barlow Condensed -> glyph absent -> Chromium per-glyph fallback (Arial Narrow / system sans)
- build: viz helper + test (instrument) -> compositions test over rendered strings seeded red on '→' -> replace the arrow -> green

## Expected impact


## Evaluation
Claim: quality - glyphs rendered outside the OFL faces
Before: 2 render-path strings use a glyph 3 of 3 faces lack; 0 gates can detect it
After: predicted 0 strings, 1 gate (missingGlyphs over rendered text) - not built: the fix site is packages/compositions (out of this round's paths)
Method: simulation - read from the generated advance table and the two call sites; the instrument is S but its consumer is out of scope
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/viz/src/font-metrics.generated.ts:7 codes end ...,8722,8592,8593,8594,8595
:16 condensed-800 row ends ...,437,0,0,0,0
:20 ui-500 row ends ...,667,0,858,0,858
:32 mono-700 row ends ...,600,0,600,0,600
packages/compositions/src/EraAdjustedFrame.tsx:279 prefix={`${ordinal(hi.raw_rank).toUpperCase()} →`}
packages/schemas/src/fixtures.ts:29 on_screen: "43rd → 1st"
instrument: packages/viz `missingGlyphs(text, face, weight)` + a compositions test over every rendered string, seeded red on the Era '→' prefix (out-of-scope: compositions)

title: Captions size lines by a 0.56 em average; viz holds real Inter metrics
body:
## Summary
packages/captions sizes burned caption lines with AVG_CHAR_EM 0.56 x chars; measured with the real Inter Bold table a 19-char upper-case line is 935 px against an 837 px box.

## Description
packages/captions/src/geometry.ts:18 and :40-41 estimate `line.length * 0.56 * fontSize`, and fitCharsPerLine gives 19 chars at 76 px vertical. packages/viz measureText (real advances from the same OFL Inter, packages/viz/src/text.ts:71) shows mixed-case lines are fine (752-764 px) but upper-case lines overflow ('MAXIMUM WORLD TITLE' 935 px > 837). One rule (does this caption line fit), two implementations; DataRace was migrated to real metrics (DESIGN.md §6.2 DataRace text fit), captions were not. Fix: captions measure with viz measureText at weight 700 (captions would depend on @statreel/viz).

## Flow
- caption cue 'MAXIMUM WORLD TITLES' -> estimateLineWidth 809 px <= 837 -> accepted
- rendered Inter Bold 76 px -> 935 px -> runs past the plate
- fix (captions context): estimateLineWidth = measureText(line, fs, 'ui', 0, 700)

## Expected impact


## Evaluation
Claim: quality - caption lines wider than the box
Before: 2 of 6 sampled 19-char lines exceed the box under real metrics while the estimate passes all 6
After: predicted 0 accepted-but-overflowing lines
Method: probe - real-metric widths of 6 sample lines vs the estimate; the fix is in packages/captions (out of scope)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/captions/src/geometry.ts:18 `export const AVG_CHAR_EM = 0.56;`
packages/captions/src/geometry.ts:40-41 `line.length * AVG_CHAR_EM * CAPTION_STYLE[format].fontSize`
probe4: "MAXIMUM WORLD TITLE" est 809 real 935 inner 837 OVERFLOWS
instrument: captions test: captionSafeZoneViolations on an upper-case 19-char cue goes red under the estimate, green under measureText (out-of-scope: captions)

title: slopegraphLayout below two rows returns non-finite geometry and no overflow
body:
## Summary
With 0 rows the layout returns leftX -Infinity / rightX Infinity and overflow false; the component would draw axis titles around nothing.

## Description
packages/viz/src/slopegraph-layout.ts:202-204 take Math.max over empty arrays (-Infinity), so plot.leftX/rightX become -Infinity/Infinity, overflow stays false, and Slopegraph still renders its axis titles (packages/viz/src/Slopegraph.tsx:121-176). Registry data-viz/empty-and-degraded-chart-states: a form's structural minimum (a slope needs two members) belongs in the component that owns the form; chrome never renders around nothing. Today the Era schema requires >= 3 rows (packages/schemas/src/index.ts:140), so it is unreachable from the shipping path. Fix: n < 2 -> finite geometry and a degenerate/overflow flag; Slopegraph renders no chrome.

## Flow
- slopegraphLayout([], ...) -> plot {leftX: -Infinity, rightX: Infinity}, overflow false
- fix: guard n < 2 in the layout, test it

## Expected impact


## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the form's structural minimum is handled in the form
Before: n=0 -> non-finite plot, overflow false (probe)
After: predicted finite plot + overflow true; not built: unreachable today, below this round's build bar
Method: probe - slopegraphLayout([]) on the real code; the fix is S but has no reachable consumer
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
probe1: empty rows: { top: 54, bottom: 584, leftX: -Infinity, rightX: Infinity } false
packages/schemas/src/index.ts:140 rows: z.array(EraRowSchema).min(3).max(12)
instrument: viz.test: slopegraphLayout with 0 and 1 rows -> finite plot and overflow true (seed red on HEAD)

title: Slopegraph axis titles are neither measured nor wrapped
body:
## Summary
The left and right axis titles render at 28 px caps with letter-spacing and are never measured, so long titles collide in the header while the sub-titles beside them are wrapped to the column.

## Description
packages/viz/src/slopegraph-layout.ts:154-161 wraps only leftSub/rightSub to colW and sizes the header for one title line; packages/viz/src/Slopegraph.tsx:124-159 draws labels.left (start-anchored) and labels.right (end-anchored, uppercase, letterSpacing 0.08 em) with no width check. The Era passes fixed short titles ('Raw rank', 'Era-adjusted rank'), so it fits today; any other caller's long title overlaps silently. Fix: measure titles with measureText at the display face, wrap or flag overflow like the sub-titles.

## Flow
- labels {left: long, right: long} -> both drawn on one line at titleY -> overlap at the centre
- fix: wrap titles to colW and grow headerHeight, or flag overflow

## Expected impact


## Evaluation
Claim: quality - header titles fit their column
Before: 0 of 2 title lines measured (sub-titles: 2 of 2)
After: predicted 2 of 2
Method: simulation - read from the layout and the component; no shipping input reaches it
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/viz/src/slopegraph-layout.ts:154-155 wrapText only for leftSub/rightSub
packages/viz/src/slopegraph-layout.ts:161 headerHeight assumes one title line
packages/viz/src/Slopegraph.tsx:133,159 labels.left/right.toUpperCase() unmeasured
instrument: viz.test: two 40-char titles at 885 px -> title boxes overlap (seed red), then wrapped/flagged
